scope: Synthetic Qt ownership mechanism only. No real data, application workflow, platform or production source changes.

primary_sources.supports: Non-main wrapper deallocation for main-thread-only types enqueues native destructor and a CPython pending call; not restricted to cyclic GC.
Deletion queue invokes each saved native destructor and then clears entries.
GUI objects belong to main thread; foreign thread deletion unsafe; deleteLater is prescribed for owner-thread event dispatch.

initial_probe_issue: First graph had a signal closure retaining table graph outside GC traversal; both modes retained all objects and collected zero. It was not a crash. Console evidence retained. Removed this extra root to test collectible cycles.
conclusions: Background cyclic collection demonstrably finalizes GUI wrappers off the GUI thread while native objects are later destroyed on GUI thread, matching the documented Shiboken delayed-deletion mechanism in the crash path.
GUI-owned cyclic collection removes that specific cross-thread wrapper-finalization route for naturally collected cycles, preserving normal reference counting.

A GUI GC coordinator is justified as targeted runtime hardening, but cannot by itself prove remediation of the original purecall: purecall was not reproduced, affected class unknown, and non-GC final reference release can still enqueue native deletion.
recommendations: Retain normal QObject parent ownership and worker wait-before-deleteLater. Do not globally remove deleteLater.

GUI GC timer must retain its QObject owner, reject non-GUI invocation and reentrancy, stop scheduling on shutdown, and perform final collection only while QApplication is still valid after workers have ended. Restore prior automatic-GC state after controlled teardown.
Use generational collection to limit UI latency; measure pauses and RSS for repeated preparation/save/page transitions, rather than assume no performance effect.
Persist Qt diagnostic messages/fatal text and native Python faulthandler output without opening widgets.
Continue to audit worker closures and result containers for GUI-wrapper final references; GUI-only cyclic GC does not solve all reference-count releases.
limitations: No original purecall was reproduced in these probes.
This test uses offscreen QApplication and synthetic widget graphs, not the full business application.
No claim that a particular progress dialog, table or model caused the original crash.
